source_uncertainties: Module 07 source: the Source slide of Module 07 was not viewed for this chapter; the chapter relies on the statement of the chapter 'Fourier modes and their evolution' that the module's slides name Pope (2000). Module 08's Source slide (L35, 190 s) was viewed.
Slide L34 f0040 prints u_hat_j(kappa') inside the sum of the evolution equation; the contraction with P_jk requires u_hat_k(kappa'). The chapter writes u_hat_k (13.1).

Slide L35 f0009 and L36 f0003 print the Fourier-pair prefactor as 1/(2 pi^3) on both transforms and omit dr, dkappa; the chapter uses chapter 8's pair (8.29)-(8.30), with (2 pi)^-3 on the forward transform only, consistent with the next slide's R_ij(0) = integral of Phi_ij.
Slide L35 f0025 writes the integrand of the shell integral as (1/2)Phi_ii S(kappa) instead of (1/2)Phi_ii dS(kappa).

Slide L35 f0023 prints the dissipation integral as epsilon = integral of 2 nu kappa^2 Phi_ii d kappa. With E = (1/2) integral of Phi_ii over the sphere and epsilon = integral of 2 nu kappa^2 E d kappa, that expression is twice the dissipation. The chapter writes epsilon = nu times the integral of kappa^2 Phi_ii, which is the limit of its (13.8) and follows from (11.4) and (8.30).
L34 19:43: the lecture ascribes the vanishing of the pairs kappa' = kappa and kappa'' = kappa to the Kronecker delta; the chapter gives the reason u_hat(0) = 0 (zero box average).
L34 22:10-22:40: the lecture gives conjugate symmetry as the reason why coefficients at kappa' != -kappa are uncorrelated; the chapter proves it from homogeneity.

L36 22:54 (speech): 'C is half C1 p times p over p plus 2'; the slide (f0023) has C = (1/2) p (2+p) C1, and the lecture's own derivation (L36 15:31) gives the slide's form. The chapter follows the slide.
L36 27:06 (speech): the closing summary says the spectra vary as kappa^2 at low wavenumbers; the slide (f0045) states it for E(kappa) only. The chapter notes the difference.
The slide's E22 curve (f0041) is a small reproduction; whether it rises slightly before falling cannot be read with certainty. The chapter says 'level, or rises slightly'.
ASR: 'copper' for kappa (L34 16:40-17:30), 'new' for nu, 'E to 2' for E22 (L36 16:06). Symbols are taken from the slides.

Practice problems: L59-P9 and T2-P12 pose the same three parts; they are merged as Exercise 8. The T2-P11 slide writes R_ij(r) = <R_ij(r)>_l, which defines R_ij through itself; the exercise uses the box average of the product of velocities. The recording states at L59 24:30 that conjugate symmetry was R_ij(-kappa) = R_ij(kappa); the slide has R_hat_ij(kappa) = R_hat_ji(-kappa).

Chapter 12 is cited by title only; the statements attributed to it (box of side 1 m, the factor 1/2 absent from its modal energy and present in its per-realization energy e_hat, R_ij periodic in r, the pair sum) were checked against the committed chapter 12 (965c68f) in gate 6b rounds 1 and 2.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.teaching_construction: Two-level model (periodic box; unbounded homogeneous field of chapter 8); jet case nu 1.4607e-5, u0 2 m/s, l0 0.1 m, Re0 1.37e4, eps 80, eta 79.0 um, k 6, Re_lambda 453 (chapter 11); box 1 m; test spectrum with C 1.5, lL 75.86 mm, beta 2.093, peak 14.4 rad/m.

sections.section: The evolution equation with the nonlinear term written out
sections.lecture_material: Recap of the pressure elimination; G_hat_j = i kappa_k sum u_hat_j(kappa') u_hat_k(kappa - kappa') by box average and orthonormality; final evolution equation; triads; non-local convection; deterministic ODEs (slides f0014, f0021, f0040, f0044).
sections.teaching_construction: Index correction u_hat_k(kappa'); reason why kappa' = kappa pairs vanish (u_hat(0) = 0).

sections.lecture_material: Neglect of convection at low Re; u_hat(kappa,t) = u_hat(kappa,0) exp(-nu kappa^2 t); high wavenumbers decay faster (f0014, f0021).
sections.teaching_construction: Energy decay (13.3); late-time law (13.4) from the low-wavenumber exponent; jet check: viscous time at the peak 164 s against turnover 0.05 s; program slope -1.500.

sections.section: The covariance of the coefficients, the kinetic energy and the dissipation
sections.lecture_material: Zero mean of coefficients; covariance uncorrelated unless kappa' = -kappa; R_hat_ij definition; E_hat = (1/2) R_hat_ii; k and eps as sums over modes (f0044, f0048).
sections.teaching_construction: Proof from homogeneity (13.5); (13.7); positive semidefiniteness and coherence bound; derivation of the dissipation sum from (11.4); the factor 1/2 against Lecture 31.

sections.section: From the box to the velocity-spectrum tensor
sections.lecture_material: Fourier pair R_ij - Phi_ij; Reynolds-stress density per unit wavenumber volume; R_ij(0) = integral Phi_ij; dimensions; three kinds of information; dissipation integral (f0009, f0021).
sections.teaching_construction: Limit R_hat_ij ~ kappa0^3 Phi_ij (13.10); dissipation integral nu times integral kappa^2 Phi_ii (the slide omits the 1/2); lattice sums for boxes 0.25, 1, 4 m (4.7002, 5.9571, 5.9993 against 6); 56 vectors below the peak in the 1 m box; shell count 3.2e5 at 1000 rad/m.

sections.section: The energy-spectrum function as an integral over spherical shells
sections.lecture_material: Half trace and integration over the sphere S(kappa); shell drawing kappa to kappa + dkappa; properties of E (real, non-negative, undefined or zero for negative kappa); k and eps integrals (f0025, f0038, f0040).
sections.teaching_construction: Equivalence with (8.32); box shell sum; shell populations (18, 62, 350) and sampling scatter N^-1/2 under a Gaussian assumption.

sections.section: In isotropic turbulence the tensor is fixed by the energy spectrum
sections.lecture_material: In general Phi_ij contains more information than E; in isotropic turbulence Phi_ij is determined by E (f0040).
sections.teaching_construction: Proof of (13.12) from reflections, rotations and incompressibility; role of reflection invariance (helical term).

sections.section: One-dimensional spectra and their relation to the energy spectrum
sections.lecture_material: E11 related to the longitudinal autocorrelation and to E by (13.14); inversion (13.16); 'this applies to other flows as well' (f0016).
sections.research_extension: Yeung and Zhou 1997, eq. (2), report p. 2: inversion as a kinematic constraint under isotropy at scale 1/kappa.
sections.teaching_construction: Definition (13.13) with the factor 1/pi; derivation of (13.14); normalization; monotonicity (13.15); derivation of (13.16); locality; share of E11 from kappa > 2 kappa1 (51 %) and > 10 kappa1 (3.9 %).

sections.section: The integral scale and the transverse spectrum
sections.lecture_material: L11 = pi E11(0)/(2<u1^2>); transverse spectrum E22 = (1/2)(E11 - kappa1 dE11/dkappa1) (f0016, f0023).
sections.research_extension: Saddoughi 1993, eq. (2), p. 237: E22 = E33 = (1/2)(1 - kappa1 d/dkappa1) E11 under isotropy (Batchelor 1953).
sections.teaching_construction: Derivation of (13.17) without isotropy; integral form of E22; L22 = L11/2; non-monotonicity of E22 (13.19); test spectrum maximum 5.66 % above E22(0) at 3.9 rad/m.

sections.section: Power laws and the constants of the three spectra
sections.lecture_material: E11 = C1 A kappa1^-p with A = <u1^2> L11^(1-p) as example; C = (1/2) p (2+p) C1; C1' = (1/2)(1+p) C1; derivation by differentiation (f0023).
sections.research_extension: Saddoughi 1993, p. 238: C = (55/18) C1, C1'/C1 = 4/3; Yeung and Zhou 1997, report p. 2: C = (55/18) C1.
sections.teaching_construction: Interval of validity (locality of (13.16)); local slopes and E/E11 of the test spectrum; normalization and the meaning of C1 (C1^(L) = 0.454); dissipation estimate (13.21): 73.6 and 13.8 against 80.

sections.lecture_material: Grid-turbulence f(r) at x1/M = 42, 98, 172 (Comte-Bellot and Corrsin 1971, as captioned); comparison figure at R_lambda = 500 from a model spectrum; four observations (f0039, f0041, f0045).
sections.teaching_construction: Figure 13.1 from the test spectrum; check of each observation; low-wavenumber exponent from the correlation (13.22).

sections.section: Executable check: the test spectrum, the one-dimensional spectra, the constants and the box
sections.teaching_construction: Program (NumPy) with exact printed output; failure test (sign of the weight in E22).

sections.section: What the relations establish and what they do not
sections.research_extension: Chapter 11's report of Saddoughi's boundary-layer test of E22/E11 = 4/3.
sections.teaching_construction: Classification of results as exact, exact under isotropy, approximate.

sections.lecture_material: Exercises 7 and 8 adapted from the practice problems T2-P11, L59-P9 and T2-P12.
